FIELD_066.context: Two facade crews share one lifting platform and are arguing about which level has priority.
FIELD_066.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will hold a meeting of the foremen and the platform operator to agree time windows.
options.B: I will propose a justified sequence and jointly confirm the platform handover times.
options.C: I will propose an order for the levels and agree it with both facade crews.
options.D: I will name the order based on the readiness of the substrates and the conditions for safe work on each level.

FIELD_067.context: The floor covering was delivered on time, but control measurements of screed moisture give different values.
FIELD_067.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will repeat the measurements using the accepted method and record the decision on readiness.
options.B: I will compare the conditions of the moisture measurements and arrange a control check before laying the covering.
options.C: I will check the instrument, the measuring points and the curing conditions, then compare the results with the material requirements.
options.D: I will document the moisture check and will not allow laying until the base is confirmed ready.

FIELD_068.context: On the trial area the texture of the decorative plaster differs noticeably from the approved sample.
FIELD_068.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will compare the texture with the sample on specific features and propose a way of showing it again myself.
options.B: I will check the tools, the mix and the application conditions to determine the cause of the difference.
options.C: I will tell the contractor directly that I do not accept continuing based on the current sample.
options.D: I will show the measurable differences and propose a new trial before agreeing any further area.

FIELD_069.context: The same remark about the skirting junction recurs on several floors.
FIELD_069.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will collect photos and batch data to find the common cause.
options.B: I will discuss the defect with the floor supervisors and installers to agree a consistent correction.
options.C: I will check the cause on one joint and, together with the crew, update the workmanship sample.
options.D: I will collect examples of the junctions from each floor and, together with the finishers, find the common source of the remarks.

FIELD_070.context: For the suspended facade panels, the as-built drawing of the fixings lags behind the actual installation by one work section.
FIELD_070.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will not hand over the section until the drawing is updated and the fixings are confirmed.
options.B: I will organise a control check on site and formalise an up-to-date drawing before handover.
options.C: I will personally organise the update of the fixing drawing and establish the procedure for handing over completed sections.
options.D: I will note that the facade as-built drawing is behind and send a request to update it before handover.

FIELD_071.context: Before handing over an apartment, the contractor sent a list of remarks without assigned owners or deadlines.
FIELD_071.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will update the register and, together with the participants, agree priorities and inspection dates.
options.B: I will agree with the contractor who will address each remark and enter the confirmed deadlines into the common register.
options.C: I will set up a single register with an owner and a deadline for each item.
options.D: I will bring together the contractors and the acceptance inspector to assign the remarks to those responsible.

FIELD_072.context: The facade contractor asks for an additional evening shift to finish the section before the rain.
FIELD_072.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will propose conditions for the evening shift and check the participants' readiness together with the contractor.
options.B: I will state the necessary conditions for lighting, permits and control, then agree the decision with the manager.
options.C: I will contact the contractor, the safety service and the inspector to assess the real shift staffing.
options.D: I will propose the shift only under confirmed conditions and establish control points together with the participants.

FIELD_073.context: The inspection certificate states one drawing number, but on site the work corresponds to a later revision.
FIELD_073.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the drawing issue log against the actual joint to determine which revision was applied.
options.B: I will return the certificate for its details to be clarified and will not sign it until the documentation is agreed.
options.C: I will check the revision on site and prepare a correct set of supporting documents before signing.
options.D: I will compare the work with the revision history and record a confirmed reference in the acceptance package.

FIELD_074.context: The contractor asks you to sign acceptance of the section today, citing an urgent payment, although one measurement has not yet been documented.
FIELD_074.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will say directly that signing is possible after a documented measurement and set a time for the check.
options.B: I will present a list of the missing data and propose that the contractor carry out the measurement promptly.
options.C: I will check the information on the undocumented measurement and personally set out the conditions for signing to the contractor.
options.D: I will check which parameter is unconfirmed and what control is required to complete acceptance.

FIELD_075.context: A similar surface defect in the concrete recurs on three pour sections after stripping.
FIELD_075.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will organise the data and, together with the participants, agree to test the hypothesis on the next section.
options.B: I will collect data on the recurring defect and, together with the supervisors, compare the conditions of the three sections.
options.C: I will compare the placement logs, mix compositions and compaction conditions to find the common factor.
options.D: I will gather the supervisors, the laboratory and the technologist for a joint analysis of the recurrence.

FIELD_076.context: The material test report lacks a reference linking the sample to the delivered batch.
FIELD_076.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will request the link between the sample and the batch myself and establish the procedure for checking the corrected report.
options.B: I will record that the report has no link between the sample and the batch and file a request to the laboratory.
options.C: I will not accept the report as confirmation for this batch until the identification is restored.
options.D: I will check the sampling documents and file a request for a corrected report before acceptance.

FIELD_077.context: Inspections of several joints due to be concealed have been requested for one shift, but the quality control service cannot get to all of them.
FIELD_077.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will record the mandatory hold points in the register and notify the sections of the windows.
options.B: I will contact the supervisors and allocate inspections according to the readiness of the joints and the availability of inspectors.
options.C: I will update the register and, together with the sections, agree a realistic inspection sequence.
options.D: I will agree the available windows with the sections and enter the confirmed sequence into the inspection register.

FIELD_078.context: The contractor sharply objects to your quality remark, and the acceptance is taking place in front of the client.
FIELD_078.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will propose looking at the joint and the documents together so that both sides understand the remark in the same way.
options.B: I will present verifiable facts and invite the contractor to agree on a method of checking.
options.C: I will present my position on the remark and invite the contractor to a joint check of the disputed joint.
options.D: I will calmly state the specific non-conformity and the evidence required, leaving the decision to quality control.

FIELD_079.context: The as-built fixing drawing shows coordinates that differ from the surveyor's control survey.
FIELD_079.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will reconcile the source data and demand an up-to-date drawing before the remark is closed.
options.B: I will compare the source data of both surveys and file a request for a confirmed fixing drawing.
options.C: I will check the coordinate system, the reference benchmarks and the dates of both surveys.
options.D: I will suspend acceptance of the drawing and file a request for it to be corrected using confirmed data.

FIELD_080.context: Photos of concealed work are attached to the certificate, but two work sections are mixed up in the file names.
FIELD_080.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check where the photos belong using visible landmarks and personally propose to the contractor a procedure for correcting the archive.
options.B: I will check the metadata, the sequence of work and the landmarks in the frames to establish which section they belong to.
options.C: I will say clearly that I cannot accept the photos as evidence without an unambiguous link.
options.D: I will show the discrepancy and propose restoring the link together using the log and the original photos.

FIELD_081.context: Within an hour, three requests to inspect joints came in from different contractors; two of the work items will be covered up immediately after inspection.
FIELD_081.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will compare the readiness and construction sequence for each inspection request.
options.B: I will contact the contractors and agree windows while keeping all joints accessible.
options.C: I will set priorities by the risk of closing up and confirm the inspection order together with the supervisors.
options.D: I will compare the readiness of the three joints and, together with the contractors, allocate time for control inspections.

FIELD_082.context: During incoming inspection of window units, it was found that the document for the required type of glazing unit belongs to a different delivery.
FIELD_082.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will not accept the document for this batch and will demand the corresponding confirmation.
options.B: I will record the mismatch and approve the units after receiving the document for the actual batch.
options.C: I will personally point out the document mismatch to the supplier and record the status of the window units until it is clarified.
options.D: I will note the delivery mismatch in the incoming inspection and file a request for the correct document.

FIELD_083.context: In the designer's supervision log, a remark was closed with a date earlier than when the contractor sent the photo of the fix.
FIELD_083.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the entries and, together with the participants, restore a provable inspection date.
options.B: I will agree confirmation of the inspection date with the participants and keep the verified chronology in the register.
options.C: I will keep the original entries and demand a verifiable chronology of the work.
options.D: I will contact the contractor and the designer's supervision to find out the source of the inconsistency.

FIELD_084.context: The client's representative asks to reduce the sample size for checking facade fixings because the handover deadline is close.
FIELD_084.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will propose my own solution to the client for organising access and discuss it with the contractor.
options.B: I will state directly that the inspection procedure changes only through an agreed programme and the responsible people.
options.C: I will discuss with the client and the contractor how to speed up access to the points without reducing the required control.
options.D: I will propose an additional team for access and keep the approved sample size.

FIELD_085.context: Wall plumbness measurements from two instruments gave different values near the limit specified in the design.
FIELD_085.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the instruments' metrological verification status, the method and the control points, then repeat the measurements.
options.B: I will not confirm acceptance until a reproducible result is obtained using the established method.
options.C: I will compare the measurement conditions, arrange a repeat survey and decide based on its data.
options.D: I will compare the conditions of the two measurements and arrange an additional measurement according to the established procedure.

FIELD_086.context: The contractor considers the cladding deviation cosmetic, but you see a possible defect in the junction detail.
FIELD_086.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will state clearly that the joint must be checked before the work is accepted.
options.B: I will show the differences from the detail and propose jointly opening up a control area by agreement.
options.C: I will compare the actual junction with the design detail and personally present the grounds for the check.
options.D: I will check the design detail and the actual workmanship, separating appearance from function.

FIELD_087.context: Control measurements of the concrete cover to the reinforcement give an inconsistent picture across different areas.
FIELD_087.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will prepare a measurement map and, together with the participants, agree a check of the areas with deviations.
options.B: I will prepare a map of cover measurements and clarify the disputed areas together with the laboratory.
options.C: I will compare the measurement points with the design, the reinforcement layout and the conditions of use of the instrument.
options.D: I will discuss with the supervisor and the laboratory a programme of additional checks in the disputed zones.

FIELD_088.context: To get approval for a material substitution, the contractor brought the manufacturer's catalogue, but there is no confirmation of a specific design requirement.
FIELD_088.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will formulate the missing material confirmations myself and include them in the approval request.
options.B: I will add the missing confirmation of the design parameter to the list of remarks on the substitution package.
options.C: I will not confirm the substitution without the designer's approval and a complete technical justification.
options.D: I will check the parameters and draw up a list of documents needed to decide on the substitution.

FIELD_089.context: Certificates for individual systems were brought for handover of a services shaft, but the overall as-built drawing has not been put together.
FIELD_089.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will draw up a list of mandatory documents and keep control over each section.
options.B: I will bring together the system contractors and the technical department (PTO) to assign preparation of the missing materials.
options.C: I will check the certificates against the actual work and, together with the participants, prepare a complete set of drawings.
options.D: I will allocate preparation of the drawings among the contractors and keep control of completeness for each section.

FIELD_090.context: A young inspector reports a possible defect but is afraid to argue with the contractor's experienced supervisor.
FIELD_090.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will go with the inspector for a joint inspection, listen to both sides and help put the facts into words.
options.B: I will state the requirement for a check and, together with the inspector, carry out the inspection and record the result.
options.C: I will suggest that the inspector and I present the facts to the supervisor together, and take responsibility for leading the discussion.
options.D: I will record the fact myself and clearly set out to the supervisor the procedure for an objective check.

FIELD_091.context: In the drawing of utility penetrations, one sleeve is shown in a different place than on the actual wall.
FIELD_091.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will formalise a measurement, check whether the change was approved and demand a correct as-built drawing.
options.B: I will compare the actual position of the sleeve with the design and record the result of checking the change.
options.C: I will check the axes, the current design and the as-built measurement, then determine the impact on the joint.
options.D: I will not sign the drawing until the actual position is approved in writing.

FIELD_092.context: During a spot check of facade cassettes, one concealed joint raises doubts about the completeness of the fasteners.
FIELD_092.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the completeness of the disputed joint and personally propose to the contractor the scope of an additional inspection.
options.B: I will check the documentation and the actual joint, then propose extending the inspection under the programme.
options.C: I will firmly demand that access be kept and that the section not be accepted until the fixing is confirmed.
options.D: I will point out my specific concern and propose a joint check of the neighbouring joints.

FIELD_093.context: After heavy rain, damp patches appeared on the facade insulation, but the contractor considers them superficial.
FIELD_093.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the type of material, the permissible storage conditions and the actual depth of wetting.
options.B: I will gather the technologist, the contractor and the inspector to agree a method of checking.
options.C: I will record the zones, check the instructions and, together with the participants, arrange a suitability check.
options.D: I will compare the wetting conditions with the material instructions and, together with the technologist, determine the method of checking.

FIELD_094.context: The contractor marked a remark as resolved, attaching a general photo of the floor in which the joint is not visible.
FIELD_094.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will not close the entry until the joint is inspected or unambiguous confirmation is received.
options.B: I will clarify the location, organise a control inspection and document the result before closing.
options.C: I will personally arrange confirmation that the joint was fixed and record the result before closing the remark.
options.D: I will record that the general photo does not confirm the specific joint and leave the remark open.

FIELD_095.context: Within a month, three contractors repeated the same mistake in concealed work certificates.
FIELD_095.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will show the typical mistakes, agree a checklist with the contractors and check the next submission.
options.B: I will agree with the contractors to review the repeated mistakes and establish an updated procedure for preparing certificates.
options.C: I will collect examples of the mistakes and update the document completeness checklist.
options.D: I will hold a short review with the contractors and the technical department (PTO) using specific examples.
